# path

> Part of the [Implementation Status](README.md) index. Node's `path` module — portable filesystem path manipulation, in both of Node's flavours: a bare `path` is the host's flavour (`path.win32` on Windows, `path.posix` elsewhere), and `path.posix` / `path.win32` name one explicitly on any host ([TDD-00178](../tdd/TDD-00178.md)). Node's own lib/path.js in TypeScript (`lib/node/path.ts`, [ADR-01290](../adr/ADR-01290.md)), with `path/posix` and `path/win32`; import-gated (`import path from 'path'`, `import { join, win32 } from 'path'`).

**Coverage**: 10/10 (100%) · **Strict Coverage**: 7/10 (70%).

Format: [Status page format](README.md#status-page-format).

| API | Status | Caveats | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path.join(...segments)` | ✅ | • A non-string argument held in `any` is converted to a string at the call instead of throwing Node's `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE` (the parameters are typed `string`) | • posix: skips empty segments, joins the rest with `/`, then normalizes (collapses repeated slashes, drops `.` segments, resolves `..` against segments already seen in the same call, and preserves a trailing slash the last segment carries — `path.join('foo', 'bar/')` is `'foo/bar/'`, matching Node)<br>• win32: Node's `join` — mixed `/`/`\` accepted and normalised to `\`, UNC roots (`\\server\share`) preserved, drive roots (`C:\`) never escaped by `..`, trailing separator kept, reserved device names (`CON`, `COM1:`) left un-normalised |
| `path.resolve(...segments)` | ✅ | • `path.win32.resolve()` on a non-Windows host resolves against a POSIX `cwd` (`/home/me` → `\home\me\foo`), exactly as Node does there; only meaningful on Windows. | • posix: absolute-always — starts from `process.cwd()`, walks segments left to right, any segment starting with `/` resets the accumulator (discarding everything before it, including cwd) — equivalent to real Node's right-to-left "stop at the last absolute segment" algorithm<br>• win32: Node's right-to-left walk with device tracking — the last device seen wins, a segment rooted on another drive discards earlier ones, a drive-relative segment (`C:x`) is resolved against that drive's own current directory (`process.env['=C:']`, falling back to `cwd`), a rooted-but-driveless segment (`\abs`) takes `cwd`'s drive |
| `path.dirname(p)` | ✅ | | • Directory portion; trailing separators trimmed first<br>• win32: a drive root (`C:\`) or UNC root (`\\server\share`) is its own dirname; the input's own separators are kept (dirname slices, never rewrites) |
| `path.basename(p, ext?)` | ✅ | | • Final path segment, optionally with a trailing `ext` stripped — not stripped when doing so would consume the whole segment, unless the *entire* `path` argument equals `ext` (then returns `""`), matching real Node's own asymmetric rule here<br>• win32: a leading `X:` device is skipped before scanning; both separators end a segment<br>• See [ADR-00368](../adr/ADR-00368.md) |
| `path.extname(p)` | ✅ | | • Extension of the basename, including the leading `.`; `""` for a dotfile whose only `.` is its first character<br>• win32: a leading `X:` device is skipped before scanning |
| `path.parse(p)` / `path.format(obj)` | ✅ | | • `parse` returns `{root, dir, base, ext, name}`; `format` is the inverse (`base` wins over `name`+`ext`, `dir` falls back to `root`)<br>• win32: `root` is `C:\`, `C:` (drive-relative), `\` or a UNC share root with its trailing separator (`\\server\share\`); `format` joins with `\` |
| `path.isAbsolute(p)` | ✅ | | • posix: `p[0] === '/'`<br>• win32: a leading `/` or `\` (including UNC), or `X:` followed by a separator; drive-relative `C:x` is not absolute |
| `path.sep` / `path.delimiter` | ✅ | | • The host's flavour: `/` and `:` on Linux/macOS, `\\` and `;` on Windows; `path.posix.sep` / `path.win32.sep` (and `delimiter`) name a flavour explicitly |
| `path.posix` / `path.win32` | ✅ | • `matchesGlob` is missing from both flavours (it needs Node's glob matcher). | • Both flavour objects exist on every host, as in Node, and are values: `path.posix.join(...)`, `const p = path.win32`, a `PlatformPath` or `typeof path.posix` parameter, `import { win32 } from 'path'`, and the `path/posix` / `path/win32` modules |
| `path.normalize(p)` / `path.relative(from, to)` / `path.toNamespacedPath(p)` | ✅ | | • Both flavours, from Node's own algorithms ([ADR-00723](../adr/ADR-00723.md)): `normalize` resolves `.`/`..` and repeated separators and **keeps a trailing separator** (`a//b/` → `a/b/`, `C:/a//b/` → `C:\a\b\`); `relative` resolves both ends against `process.cwd()` first and walks up with `..` (win32 compares case-insensitively and returns `to` outright across drives or UNC shares); `toNamespacedPath` is the identity for posix and, for win32, the resolved `\\?\C:\…` / `\\?\UNC\…` long-path form |
